text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber warns against softening the stability criteria for the launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU). Finance Minister Theo Waigel is opposed to delay in EMU
- Pay talks conflict in east German building trade escalates. Trade unions announce strike on Berlin building sites
- Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer recommends Wim Duisenburg, the future head of the European Monetary Institute, as head of the European Central Bank
HANDELSBLATT
- BDI German industry federation president Hans-Olaf Henkel demands priority for German firms says new tax bill does not help them
- Among top German firms less was earnt this year than in 1996
- DGB German trades union federation sharply criticises Bonn over budget gaps
- Finance experts' optimism for a punctual start of EMU has become clouded. Finance experts asked by Handelsblatt said the timetable had a 73 percent chance of being kept

- German Environmental Minister Angela Merkel said she regretted the failure of European countries including Germany to push through environmental reforms at a United Nations meeting in New York last week, saying the United States was responsible for this
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber wants to block Europe's planned single currency, the euro, in the Bundesrat upper house of parliament
- Hans Peter Stihl, head of the DIHT German chambers of commerce, demands a return to a 40-hour week

- North Rhine-Westfalia state finance minister Heinz Schleusser backs up Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber and Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schoeder. Stability of euro must take precedence over the timetable for EMU, the SPD politician Schleusser said
- The German constitutional court in Karlsruhe will rule on four-year row over imported bananas into the European Union
- Wim Duisenburg takes over from Alexandre Lamfalussy as head of the European Monetary Institute
DIE WELT
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber steps up row over the euro and demands a clear reply from Chancellor Helmut Kohl on the issue
- Good prospects for the Eurofighter jet project to start, according to Defence Minister Volker Ruehe
- Holidaymakers are counting their pennies when they book holidays. Small travel companies fight over each customer
- Municipal and local authorities are dragging their heels over preparing for the switch to Europe's planned currency, the euro

- No chance of reaching an agreement in row between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition and opposition Social Democrats, who are set to block the tax bill in the Bundesrat upper house of parliament --Bonn Newsroom +49 228 260 97160
